question: Window-0 / slow-read stall harness: does the AEGIS transport wrapper (per-stream 10 s stall deadline, 30 s idle, per-connection memory ledger) bound per-connection memory to M_conn = 16 MiB (TBI-7) and reap stalls (TBI-8) with the golden h2 settings (max_concurrent_streams 100, send buffer 400 KiB), or must the stream cap drop?
flips_if: wrapper does not bound memory -> lower stream cap (ARCHITECTURE 3.1 Reverse: measured cost makes TBI-7 exceed 16 MiB/connection -> lower the stream cap)

measured.hardware: laptop i9-14900HX (32 threads, 31 GiB), Linux 6.17.0-14, glibc 2.39, rustc 1.99.1, loopback TCP, h2c prior knowledge (no TLS); server and attacker on the same host under ci/heavy.sh (6 GB cgroup cap); 2026-10-25
measured.stack: hyper 1.12.0, h2 0.4.20, tokio 1.54.1, hyper-util 0.1.21 (golden lock targets); golden settings: max_concurrent_streams 100, stream/conn window 256 KiB / 1 MiB, max_frame 16384, max_send_buf 400 KiB, max_header_list 16384, max_pending_accept_reset_streams 20, keepalive 20 s/20 s (hyper)
measured.attack_window0: SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=0, 100 streams/conn, never WINDOW_UPDATE: h2 buffers 0 B; hyper holds exactly one pre-polled 16 KiB frame per stream = 1.56 MiB/conn (peak dRSS 1.71-2.02 MiB/conn at 1/10/100 conns). Memory bounded, but baseline streams are never reaped (10000 live streams at 100 conns for the whole 25 s hold)
measured.attack_bigwin_noread: large stream window (16 MiB) + one connection WINDOW_UPDATE (+1 GiB), 100 streams, then stop reading TCP: exact in-stack buffered bytes per conn: hyper 40.64 MiB, h2-direct 39.07 MiB (= 100 x 400 KiB send buffer); peak dRSS/conn hyper 42.38/41.72/41.72 MiB and h2 40.91/40.27/40.12 MiB at 1/10/100 conns; server RSS 45.7 / 420.6 / 4175.8 MiB (hyper). Never reaped. A second wave of 100 conns at t=12 s OOM-killed the h2 baseline at 5.5 GiB RSS (journal: oom-kill, 6 GB cgroup)
measured.attack_slowread: same as bigwin but drains ~1 KiB/s + 256 B WINDOW_UPDATEs: identical to bigwin (hyper 41.84 MiB/conn, 10 conns: 421.8 MiB)
measured.wrapper_prototype: h2-direct + exact per-connection ledger (bytes handed to h2 minus bytes written to socket, budget 12 MiB) + 10 s per-stream stall reset (ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM) + 30 s idle close; stream cap kept at 100: max buffered/conn 12.05 MiB at 1/10/100 conns; peak dRSS/conn 13.21 / 12.73 / 12.53 MiB (<= 16 MiB); all 100/1000/10000 stalled streams reaped at t~11 s (10 s after last progress); idle connections closed at ~31 s; slow-read 12.74 MiB/conn, reaped
measured.reaped_memory_reuse: wrapper, 100 conns, second wave of 100 conns after wave 1 was reaped: RSS peak 1258.6 MiB (wave 1) -> 1298.7 MiB (both waves, 200 live conns) instead of ~2.5 GiB: h2 frees reset streams' buffers; the post-reap RSS plateau is glibc retention, reused
measured.rapid_reset: 100 x (HEADERS+RST_STREAM) per conn, 10 conns, and 1000 per conn: hyper and h2 send GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM (11) on 27/30 conns at burst 100 and 3/3 at burst 1000 (h2 max_pending_accept_reset_streams=20 fires below the TBI-5 bucket burst of 100); dRSS 0.06-0.08 MiB/conn
measured.continuation_flood: HEADERS without END_HEADERS + 64 x 15 KiB CONTINUATION: GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM (11) on 10/10 conns, dRSS 0.08 MiB/conn (h2 header-list cap holds; not a TBI-7 risk)
measured.stream_cap_needed_without_ledger: send-buffer-bound cost is 0.417-0.424 MiB/stream peak dRSS under hyper -> floor(16 / 0.424) = 37 streams (40 by pure 16 MiB / 400 KiB arithmetic); alternatively keep 100 streams and cut max_send_buf_size to <= ~130 KiB ((16 MiB - ~1.1 MiB fixed) / 100 - one 16 KiB pre-polled frame)

decision_effect: max_concurrent_streams stays 100 and the 400 KiB send buffer stays, CONDITIONAL on the wrapper carrying an exact per-connection send ledger. Add to ARCHITECTURE 3.1 'AEGIS wrapper' list: 'per-connection send ledger: a response chunk is handed to h2 only while (bytes handed - bytes written to the socket) + chunk <= 12 MiB (M_conn 16 MiB minus measured fixed state); a stream with no send progress for 10 s, for any reason (peer window, TCP backpressure, ledger exhaustion), is reset with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM; a connection with no stream progress for 30 s is closed.' Without that ledger the golden config buffers 40.6 MiB/conn (2.5x TBI-7) and the cap would have to be 37 (or max_send_buf <= ~130 KiB). Spec notes for the integrator: (1) TBI-6 as written ('buffered bytes <= advertised connection window') is satisfied by the bigwin attack (peer advertised ~1 GiB) yet 40 MiB is buffered, so TBI-6 does not imply TBI-7; the bound must be min(peer window, local ledger budget). (2) hyper pre-polls one body frame per stream regardless of window (16 KiB x 100 = 1.56 MiB/conn under window 0), so a literal TBI-6 needs a slack of one max_frame per open stream if it is measured above hyper. (3) h2's max_pending_accept_reset_streams=20 already GOAWAYs open+immediate-RST bursts below the TBI-5 bucket burst of 100; the bucket only governs resets of accepted streams.
rung: R1 executed; measurement grade B (laptop loopback standing in for a VPS; one host for server and attacker)

limits: Wrapper prototype is on h2 directly, not behind hyper; porting it to hyper needs a counting IO plus a ledger-gated Body (poll_frame returns Pending, then Err on stall so hyper resets) - designed, not measured. Kernel socket send buffers (loopback autotune up to 4 MiB tcp_wmem) are outside RSS and outside the ledger, so they need an explicit SO_SNDBUF cap. Ledger counts DATA payload only (9 B frame headers excluded). Cleartext h2c: TLS record buffers (~tens of KiB/conn) not included. No per-stream fairness inside a saturated ledger (a connection whose ledger is full stalls all its streams and then reaps them). Post-reap RSS shows glibc retention; reuse was shown by a second wave, not by allocator trimming. Crate ages taken from supply-chain/lock-targets.toml (re-verified 2026-10-25); crates.io was not reachable from the sandbox. Loopback only: real RTT and WAN loss are not modelled. TBI-8 stall/idle timing checked by wall clock in one run per shape, not by DST.
